requirements.statement: A customer can submit a support ticket describing their issue

criteria.must: A customer can submit a ticket with their email, a subject, and a body without signing in
A submitted ticket with a missing required field is rejected

requirements.statement: Incoming tickets are automatically classified by urgency

criteria.must: A newly submitted ticket is assigned an urgency level without any human action
The assigned urgency is one of a fixed set of levels

requirements.statement: A support agent sees their queue of tickets sorted by urgency

criteria.must: A signed-in support agent can view a queue listing tickets
The queue can be filtered or ordered so the most urgent tickets are seen first
A user who is not signed in as a support agent cannot view the queue

requirements.statement: An AI-drafted reply is prepared for each ticket

criteria.must: Each ticket has a drafted reply available before a support agent writes anything
The drafted reply addresses the content the customer wrote

requirements.statement: A support agent can review and edit a drafted reply before it is sent

criteria.must: A support agent can view the full text of a ticket's drafted reply
A support agent can change the text of a drafted reply before approving it
An edited reply retains the edited text rather than reverting to the original draft

requirements.statement: A support agent can approve a reply so that it is sent to the customer

criteria.must: A support agent can mark a ticket's reply as approved
A reply is never sent to a customer without a support agent's approval

requirements.statement: The customer receives the approved reply by email

criteria.must: Once a support agent approves a reply, an email is sent to the ticket's customer email address
The emailed reply matches the approved (possibly edited) text, not the original AI draft if it was changed
